question: Did a bounded public-source search locate the 2016, 12-site fish assessment or its underlying station/specimen table cited by the AWTIP Tunnel 5 EPRMP?

boundedSearch.approach: Searched indexed public sources using the project and locality names, the EPRMP's stated 2016/12-site/17-species figures, and distinctive table-name combinations. Checked official EMB and ADB search results and publisher-hosted Norzagaray fish research. The official EMB project page and direct EPRMP PDF remain access-gated in this environment; no access control was bypassed.
queryFamilies: Norzagaray / Angat River fish survey 2016, 12 sites, 17 species
AWTIP / Tunnel 4 / Tunnel 5 2016 fish assessment and freshwater ecology
Distinctive source-table combinations including Eleotris fusca, Ophieleotris aporos, and Labeo rohita
Exact EPRMP comparison-table heading and publisher/institution repository variants
boundedSearch.result: Search results led to the 2022 AWTIP Tunnel 5 EPRMP and its indexed copies, project-construction material, and the separate 2017 Norzagaray River Glossogobius morphometrics paper. No independently identifiable 2016 report, citation, station/specimen matrix, voucher list, supplement, or accession table was located. A bounded search cannot establish that no such material exists.
boundedSearch.outreach: No government agency, author, university, or project proponent was contacted.

nearMatchAssessment.whatItReports: Portillo et al. (2017) describe 116 BFAR-authenticated Glossogobius giuris morphometric samples across five named Norzagaray River stations: Kanyakan, Calumpang, Matictic Ibayo, Bakas, and Laog.
nearMatchAssessment.limits: The reviewed article does not state the fish collection date or identify its survey as the AWTIP 2016, 12-site survey. Its received date is not a field date. It is a one-species morphometric sample and cannot supply the missing 17-taxon checklist or represent all 12 reported stations.
nearMatchAssessment.relationship: Geographic and topic overlap make it a candidate for future lineage checking only. No shared station list, specimen identifiers, project attribution, dates, vouchers, or source crosswalk establish that it is the same dataset or an independent confirmation. Keep it separate.

eprmpComparisonReconciliation.unresolved: The indexed EPRMP comparison matrix exposes 15 rows, each marked for 2016, while its prose says the 2016 study identified 17 species. The two unshown taxa, the original source, field dates, method, station identities, specimen evidence, and reuse terms remain unknown.
eprmpComparisonReconciliation.absenceRule: Do not interpret rows missing from the comparison matrix as evidence that taxa were absent in 2016; the matrix itself is incomplete against the report's aggregate claim.

reuseAndDisposition.reuse: No item-specific reuse permission was established for the 2016 comparison material. The 2017 article's separate CC Attribution notice does not grant rights to the EPRMP or any putative 2016 assessment.
reuseAndDisposition.decision: Retain the 2016 claims as an unresolved, attributed lead. Keep the 2017 goby study separate. Do not reconstruct the two missing names, infer a 2016 occurrence matrix, or merge either dataset into a current checklist.

nextAction: Continue Central Luzon freshwater coverage using separately attributable, locality-resolved sources. Revisit the 2016 AWTIP lineage only if a public, independently reviewable citation, report, specimen table, voucher record, or author-hosted supplement becomes available.

sources.supports: Officially hosted indexed EPRMP text. Its comparison paragraph states 12 sites and 17 taxa for the 2016 study; Table 2.2-20 exposes 15 2016-marked rows. This is the source making the comparison claims, not the underlying 2016 assessment.

Publisher-hosted 2017 Norzagaray River morphometrics article, including five station names, 116 goby samples, BFAR authentication, and no reported field collection date or link to the AWTIP comparison survey.
The prior official-indexed-text review of Tunnel 5 methods, site/date scope, eel interview status, and table conflicts.
The existing review of the distinct one-species Norzagaray morphometrics sample and its evidence limits.
